title: Kubermeister settings
description: The settings file, ~/.config/kubermeister/settings.json. Every key is optional; a missing one takes its default.

version.description: The shape the file is written in. Optional; the app adds it when it first saves.

general.description: Preferences about the app itself rather than about a cluster.

confirmQuit.description: Ask before quitting, since quitting ends every port forward, shell session, log follow and drain at once.

restoreOnLaunch.description: Reopen on the context and namespace last used; when false, follow the kubeconfig's current-context.

kubeconfigPath.description: The kubeconfig file to read; null reads $KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config.

data.description: How often screens refresh, how long a cluster read may take, and how much a console keeps.

refreshIntervalSec.description: Seconds between polls of the live lists, metrics and the dashboard.

readTimeoutSec.description: Seconds one cluster read may take before it is reported as timed out.

logBufferLines.description: Log lines a live follow keeps before dropping the oldest.

terminalFontSize.description: Font size of the shell terminals, in points.

updates.description: How far the updater goes on its own.

mode.description: "check" finds new versions and asks before downloading, "download" fetches them in the background, "off" checks only when asked; null follows the default, which is "download".

network.description: How cluster traffic reaches the API server.

proxyMode.description: "env" follows HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY the way kubectl does, "manual" uses proxyUrl, "off" connects directly. A context whose kubeconfig sets proxy-url always uses that.

proxyUrl.description: The proxy used under "manual", as an http, https or socks URL; null means none.

noProxy.description: Hosts that never go through a proxy, spelled as NO_PROXY spells them; null follows NO_PROXY.

caBundlePath.description: A PEM file of extra certificate authorities to trust for cluster TLS, added to the ones already trusted.

charts.description: Helm chart repositories and OCI registries.

repositories.description: Chart sources: a classic repository by its https URL, or an OCI registry by oci://host. Credentials are added in Settings and kept in the system keychain, never here.
